answer: Hardware remote attestation mitigates Sybil attacks by anchoring each agent to a discrete physical coprocessor. At the dawn of every consensus round, an agent must present an attestation quote signed by its silicon root of trust, preventing a zephyr of virtual bots from claiming seats. The verifiable cost incurred per identity is procuring a dedicated security chip no larger than a walnut. A key limitation is that hardware side-channel attacks can extract private keys to forge valid quotes.
